schema_lineage.purpose: Evaluate vendors providing Managed Detection and Response (MDR) services - encompassing standard TDIR, preemptive threat intelligence, autonomous deception, disinformation security, IR support, AI adoption in operations and development, service governance, and composable pricing model maturity.

mdr_services_taxonomy_v1.0.intent: Assess MDR vendor capability alignment across eight capability pillars and a separate pricing model evaluation scale. The capability assessment covers standard detection and response through advanced AI-driven preemptive and emerging capabilities. The pricing model assessment evaluates commercial construct maturity based on Gartner's composable pricing framework. Vendors are evaluated on demonstrated, publicly verifiable capability - not marketing claims. AI maturity within MDR operations is assessed comprehensively as both an operational dimension and a development investment dimension.

metadata.framework_alignment: Gartner MDR Market Guide + Preemptive Security / CTEM Framework + MITRE ATT&CK + NIST CSF 2.0 + Gartner Composable Pricing Research (G00826132 / G00846386)

capability_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of capability in this area

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No publicly verifiable evidence of capability in this sub-pillar.
scoring_logic.1: Minimal: Basic or manual capability; no automation, analytics, or continuous operation.
scoring_logic.2: Generic Claims: Marketing mentions the capability but lacks named products, technical docs, metrics, or specifics.
scoring_logic.3: Demonstrated: Documented capability with named products or features, some technical detail, and identifiable use cases.
scoring_logic.4: Advanced: Named products with measurable outcomes, integration points, customer validation, or analyst recognition. Automation and continuous operation present.
scoring_logic.5: Market-Leading: Best-in-class capability with deep technical evidence, extensive customer base, analyst leadership recognition, measurable impact metrics, and continuous innovation.

pricing_scoring_scale.meaning_of_zero: No publicly verifiable evidence of this pricing construct

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No public information available about this pricing dimension.
scoring_logic.1: Opaque: Pricing exists but is entirely opaque - no public detail on structure, components, or methodology.
scoring_logic.2: Basic: General pricing information available but limited transparency - bundled quotes without component breakdown.
scoring_logic.3: Structured: Defined pricing structure with identifiable components, documented on website or in sales materials.
scoring_logic.4: Transparent & Flexible: Clear component-based pricing with published tiers, calculators, or configurators. Demonstrated client flexibility.
scoring_logic.5: Composable Best Practice: Fully composable pricing model with transparent subscription, usage, fixed, and success-fee components. Real-time usage dashboards, documented KPI alignment, and demonstrated risk-sharing mechanisms.

source_policy.description: Evidence must be publicly accessible and verifiable.

coverage_grade.description: Letter grade based on percentage of capability sub-pillars covered (score ≥ 1)

mdr_service_type.Pureplay MDR: Organizations whose primary business is managed detection and response services.
mdr_service_type.Extended MDR: MDR as a core offering within a broader managed security services portfolio.
mdr_service_type.Platform MDR: Technology vendors who offer MDR services built atop their own detection platform (EDR/XDR).
mdr_service_type.IR-Enhanced MDR: MDR providers with significant incident response retainer and DFIR capabilities.

ir_focus_type.Core Competency: Incident response is a primary service line with dedicated DFIR specialists.
ir_focus_type.Assistance Component: Incident response provided as a support layer or feature within the MDR contract.

delivery_model.Platform Only: Vendor sells the detection/response platform directly to the end customer. The customer is responsible for operating, managing, and staffing the platform themselves. No managed service layer is included.
delivery_model.Platform + Partner: Vendor provides the underlying detection/response platform and works with MSSP partners who leverage that platform to deliver a managed service to the end customer. The partner operates the platform on behalf of the client.
delivery_model.Managed Service: Vendor delivers both the platform and the operational service as a unified offering. The service includes the technology, the SOC analysts, and the operational workflow. The customer consumes a fully managed outcome, not a product.

TDR.name: Standard Threat Detection, Investigation & Response
TDR.focus: Core MDR baseline - real-time signal correlation across endpoints, networks, identities, and cloud environments; alert triage and false positive identification; guided investigation; and actionable response with measurable MTTD and MTTR outcomes.
evidence_signals: 24/7 real-time signal correlation across multi-source telemetry (EDR, NDR, SIEM, cloud, identity)
Alert triage with false positive identification and noise reduction
Guided investigation capabilities with root cause determination
Response orchestration including containment, isolation, and remediation actions
Measurable SLAs for Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) and Mean Time to Respond (MTTR)

PTI.name: Preemptive Threat Intelligence
PTI.focus: AI-driven predictive analytics and threat intelligence operationalization - historically the domain of specialized threat research companies (e.g., Recorded Future) but now increasingly achievable through domain-specific AI agents and LLMs. Includes behavior-based prioritization, anomaly detection, and rapid processing of massive threat intelligence feeds.
evidence_signals: Automated threat intelligence ingestion, correlation, and actioning from multiple feeds
Predictive analytics using historical data and ML to forecast threats and vulnerabilities
Behavior-based prioritization and user/entity anomaly detection (UEBA)
TTP mapping to MITRE ATT&CK framework with proactive blocking
Intelligence-driven hunting query generation and campaign tracking

ADA.name: Autonomous Deception & AMTD
ADA.focus: Proactive, preventative stance using AI-powered analytics to create decoy environments, fake data, and misleading network traffic to expose adversary TTPs - combined with dynamic mutation of the attack surface to complicate exploitation and increase attacker cost.
evidence_signals: Decoy environments, honeypots, honeytokens, and breadcrumbs for high-fidelity detection
Automated moving target defense through runtime mutation of configurations
Dynamic attack surface management and micro-segmentation
AI-powered analytics to trick attackers into revealing TTPs
Counter-adversary operations including takedowns and adversary infrastructure disruption

DIS.name: Disinformation & Identity Security
DIS.focus: Emerging capability to detect and respond to disinformation campaigns including deepfakes, voice/image impersonation, identity fraud, and narrative attacks that evade traditional detection - protecting organizational reputation and executive identity.
evidence_signals: Deepfake and synthetic media detection capabilities
Voice, image, and identity impersonation defense
Narrative attack and social engineering detection
Brand and executive protection services
Digital risk protection and dark web monitoring for impersonation threats

IRA.name: IR Support & Assistance
IRA.focus: MDR-adjacent incident response capability modeled as the 'Assistance Component' - IR as a feature within MDR contracts rather than pureplay DFIR. Includes scoping, containment support, recovery guidance, and post-incident review, leveraging context from the DFIR capability taxonomy.
evidence_signals: Incident scoping and triage capabilities within MDR service
Containment and isolation support with evidence preservation
Recovery and restoration guidance for impacted systems
Post-incident review with root cause analysis and improvement recommendations
Integration with external DFIR specialists and retainer services

AIO.name: AI Adoption in MDR Operations
AIO.focus: Comprehensive assessment of how AI is embedded across the MDR service delivery lifecycle - from detection engineering through investigation, triage, response automation, and transparency. Evaluates whether AI delivers measurable operational improvements or remains marketing claims.
evidence_signals: AI-driven detection engineering with reduced false positive rates
AI-assisted investigation and automated triage of well-known issues
AI-powered response automation replacing traditional SOAR functions
Explainable AI outputs with transparency into methodology and reasoning
Measurable impact: increased throughput, expanded coverage, improved MTTD/MTTR

AID.name: AI Development & Platform Maturity
AID.focus: The vendor's investment in AI platform development - domain-specific LLMs, model governance, AI supply chain trustworthiness, and innovation pipeline. Evaluates whether AI capability is a genuine engineering investment or superficial marketing overlay.
evidence_signals: Domain-specific AI/LLM development for security operations
AI model governance including lifecycle management and versioning
AI supply chain assurance and third-party model risk management
Investment in AI-driven service innovation beyond traditional SOAR replacement
Published AI research, patents, or conference contributions demonstrating depth

SOG.name: Service Operations & Governance
SOG.focus: Operational maturity of the MDR service - analyst staffing model, coverage depth, compliance alignment, reporting quality, client engagement transparency, and the overall governance framework that ensures consistent, accountable service delivery.
evidence_signals: 24/7 SOC operations with documented analyst staffing model and tier structure
Client engagement model with dedicated contacts and transparent escalation paths
Compliance and regulatory alignment (SOC 2, ISO 27001, sector-specific requirements)
Quality reporting with actionable metrics, dashboards, and executive summaries
Documented service governance framework with SLAs, reviews, and continuous improvement

TDR-01.name: Signal Correlation & Alert Triage
TDR-01.expanded_definition: Real-time correlation of security signals across multi-source telemetry - endpoints (EDR), networks (NDR), cloud environments, identity providers, and SIEM platforms - with intelligent alert triage that separates actionable threats from noise.
what_to_verify_publicly: Multi-source telemetry ingestion (EDR, NDR, SIEM, cloud, identity)
Real-time signal correlation across disparate data sources
Alert prioritization with context enrichment
False positive identification and noise reduction metrics
Volume of alerts processed and triage SLAs

TDR-02.name: Investigation & Root Cause Analysis
TDR-02.expanded_definition: Guided investigation capabilities that determine the root cause, scope, and impact of detected threats - including timeline reconstruction, artifact correlation, and attack chain mapping to understand the full adversary path.
what_to_verify_publicly: Guided investigation workflows for analysts and clients
Root cause determination and attack chain reconstruction
Timeline and artifact correlation across systems
Scope and impact assessment for validated threats
Investigation documentation and knowledge base

TDR-03.name: Response Orchestration & Containment
TDR-03.expanded_definition: Actionable response capabilities including automated and human-initiated containment, isolation, and remediation actions - orchestrated across the client's security stack with documented response playbooks.
what_to_verify_publicly: Automated response actions (host isolation, account lockout, IP blocking)
Human-in-the-loop response approval workflows
Response playbook library and customization capabilities
Integration with client security tools for response execution
Response SLAs and documented containment timelines

TDR-04.name: SLA & MTTD/MTTR Performance
TDR-04.expanded_definition: Measurable service level commitments for detection and response speed - including published Mean Time to Detect (MTTD), Mean Time to Respond (MTTR), and adherence to contractual SLAs with transparent performance reporting.
what_to_verify_publicly: Published MTTD and MTTR metrics or commitments
Contractual SLAs for detection, investigation, and response phases
Performance reporting and trend tracking over time
Client-facing dashboards showing real-time SLA adherence
Third-party or analyst validation of performance claims

PTI-01.name: Threat Intelligence Operationalization
PTI-01.expanded_definition: Automated ingestion, correlation, and actioning of tactical and operational threat intelligence from multiple feeds - transforming raw intelligence into proactive blocking rules, hunting queries, and detection engineering improvements.
what_to_verify_publicly: Threat intelligence platform or feed integration capabilities
Automated IOC ingestion and correlation across telemetry
Intelligence-to-detection pipeline (feeds → rules → detections)
TTP mapping to MITRE ATT&CK framework
Automated blocking or alerting based on threat intelligence

PTI-02.name: Predictive Threat Analytics
PTI-02.expanded_definition: AI and ML-driven predictive analytics that use historical attack data, vulnerability trends, and environmental context to forecast likely threats, prioritize defensive actions, and preempt attacks before they materialize.
what_to_verify_publicly: Predictive models using historical data to forecast threats
Vulnerability trend analysis and exploitability prediction
Environmental risk scoring based on client-specific context
Proactive defensive recommendations based on predictions
Validation of prediction accuracy and effectiveness metrics

PTI-03.name: Behavior-Based Anomaly Detection
PTI-03.expanded_definition: User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) that establish baselines and detect anomalous activities across user accounts, network traffic, and system behaviors - identifying insider threats, compromised credentials, and lateral movement.
what_to_verify_publicly: UEBA capabilities with behavioral baseline establishment
Anomaly detection across user, entity, and network behaviors
Insider threat detection and compromised credential identification
Lateral movement detection through behavioral analysis
Reduction in false positives through behavioral context

PTI-04.name: Dark Web & Adversary Tracking
PTI-04.expanded_definition: Monitoring of dark web forums, threat actor communications, leaked credential databases, and adversary infrastructure - providing early warning of targeted campaigns, data exposure, and emerging threats specific to the client's environment.
what_to_verify_publicly: Dark web monitoring and intelligence gathering capabilities
Leaked credential and data exposure alerting
Adversary campaign tracking and attribution
Early warning services for client-specific threats
Integration with detection engineering for proactive defense

ADA-01.name: Deception Technology & Honeypots
ADA-01.expanded_definition: Deployment and management of decoys, honeypots, honeytokens, and breadcrumbs across client environments to detect lateral movement, credential theft, and reconnaissance with high-fidelity, low-false-positive alerts.
what_to_verify_publicly: Managed deception technology deployment within MDR service
Honeypot and honeytoken capabilities across network, endpoint, and cloud
Breadcrumb placement for lateral movement detection
High-fidelity alerting with near-zero false positive rates
Integration with MDR detection and response workflows

ADA-02.name: Automated Moving Target Defense
ADA-02.expanded_definition: Dynamic mutation and randomization of the client's IT environment - including runtime application protection, network topology reconfiguration, credential rotation, and API endpoint obfuscation - to deny adversaries a stable target.
what_to_verify_publicly: AMTD capabilities within the MDR service offering
Runtime mutation of network configurations or application environments
Dynamic micro-segmentation and topology changes
Automated credential and session rotation
Evidence of increased attacker cost through dynamic defense

ADA-03.name: Dynamic Attack Surface Management
ADA-03.expanded_definition: Continuous discovery, assessment, and dynamic reduction of the external and internal attack surface - identifying shadow IT, misconfigured cloud resources, and exposed services with automated remediation recommendations.
what_to_verify_publicly: External attack surface management (EASM) within MDR
Continuous asset discovery including shadow IT and cloud resources
Automated exposure assessment and risk scoring
Dynamic attack surface reduction recommendations
Integration with MDR detection pipeline for exposure-informed alerting

ADA-04.name: Counter-Adversary Operations
ADA-04.expanded_definition: Active measures to attribute, track, and disrupt adversary campaigns - including takedown services for phishing infrastructure and impersonation domains, adversary infrastructure mapping, and proactive threat hunting operations.
what_to_verify_publicly: Takedown service capabilities (domains, phishing, infrastructure)
Adversary infrastructure mapping and campaign tracking
Proactive hypothesis-driven threat hunting operations
Managed threat hunting with documented methodologies
Hunt findings feeding back to detection engineering improvements

DIS-01.name: Deepfake & Synthetic Media Detection
DIS-01.expanded_definition: Technical capabilities to detect AI-generated synthetic content - including deepfake video and audio, AI-generated images, and synthetic text - that may be used in social engineering, fraud, or disinformation campaigns targeting the organization.
what_to_verify_publicly: Deepfake detection technology or service capability
Synthetic audio and voice clone detection
AI-generated image and video analysis
Integration with communication security controls
False positive/negative rates for synthetic content detection

DIS-02.name: Identity Impersonation Defense
DIS-02.expanded_definition: Detection and prevention of identity-based impersonation attacks - including business email compromise (BEC), executive impersonation, account takeover, and credential stuffing - using behavioral analytics and identity verification technologies.
what_to_verify_publicly: Business email compromise (BEC) detection and prevention
Executive impersonation alerting and verification
Account takeover detection through behavioral analytics
Identity verification and authentication anomaly detection
Integration with identity providers and email security gateways

DIS-03.name: Narrative & Social Engineering Detection
DIS-03.expanded_definition: Identification of coordinated disinformation narratives and advanced social engineering campaigns targeting the organization - including influence operations, fake review campaigns, and manipulation of public perception.
what_to_verify_publicly: Social engineering campaign detection capabilities
Narrative attack identification and tracking
Influence operation monitoring and alerting
Phishing campaign analysis beyond traditional email scanning
Employee awareness and resilience assessment

DIS-04.name: Brand & Executive Protection
DIS-04.expanded_definition: Monitoring and protection of organizational brand reputation and executive digital identities - including domain squatting detection, social media impersonation, and proactive defense against reputation-damaging campaigns.
what_to_verify_publicly: Brand monitoring across web, social media, and dark web
Domain squatting and typosquatting detection
Social media impersonation monitoring and takedown
Executive digital identity protection services
Reputation threat alerting and response workflows

IRA-01.name: Incident Scoping & Triage
IRA-01.expanded_definition: Rapid assessment of incident scope, severity, and priority within the MDR service context - determining affected systems, initial impact assessment, evidence identification, and escalation decisions aligned with the client's incident response plan.
what_to_verify_publicly: Incident scoping and severity assessment capabilities
Affected system and data identification processes
Evidence preservation guidance during initial triage
Escalation criteria and decision frameworks
Integration with client incident response plans and retainers

IRA-02.name: Containment & Isolation Support
IRA-02.expanded_definition: Active containment and isolation assistance performed within or directed by the MDR service - including host isolation, network segmentation, account suspension, and lateral movement blocking while preserving forensic evidence.
what_to_verify_publicly: Remote host isolation and quarantine capabilities
Network-level containment actions (blocking, segmentation)
Account and credential suspension or reset
Evidence preservation during containment actions
Containment SLAs and documented response times

IRA-03.name: Recovery & Restoration Guidance
IRA-03.expanded_definition: Guidance and support for restoring impacted systems to operational status - including backup integrity verification, system rebuild recommendations, eradication of persistence mechanisms, and validation that the threat has been fully eliminated.
what_to_verify_publicly: Recovery guidance and restoration support within MDR
Backup integrity verification and contamination checking
Persistence mechanism identification and eradication support
System rebuild and hardening recommendations
Post-recovery validation and monitoring

IRA-04.name: Post-Incident Review & Reporting
IRA-04.expanded_definition: Structured post-incident review process that documents findings, identifies root causes, provides improvement recommendations, and updates detection engineering - ensuring the organization is better prepared for future incidents.
what_to_verify_publicly: Post-incident review (PIR) or after-action review (AAR) service
Root cause analysis with documented findings
Improvement recommendations for people, process, and technology
Detection engineering updates based on incident learnings
Executive and technical reporting for different audiences

AIO-01.name: AI in Detection Engineering
AIO-01.expanded_definition: Application of AI and ML to improve detection rule creation, tuning, and maintenance - including automated detection content generation, ML-driven false positive reduction, and continuous detection coverage assessment against MITRE ATT&CK.
what_to_verify_publicly: AI-assisted detection rule creation and tuning
ML-driven false positive reduction with measurable improvement
Automated detection coverage assessment against frameworks
AI-powered anomaly detection models in production
Detection engineering metrics showing AI impact

AIO-02.name: AI in Investigation & Triage
AIO-02.expanded_definition: AI-powered investigation assistance that accelerates analyst workflows - including automated alert triage, AI-generated investigation summaries, context enrichment, and intelligent case prioritization that replaces traditional SOAR-level automation.
what_to_verify_publicly: AI-automated alert triage for well-known issue classes
AI-generated investigation summaries and recommendations
Intelligent context enrichment from multiple data sources
Case prioritization using ML-based risk scoring
Measurable improvement in investigation speed and quality

AIO-03.name: AI in Response Automation
AIO-03.expanded_definition: AI-driven response automation that goes beyond traditional SOAR playbooks - including autonomous resolution of specific incident classes, adaptive response selection based on context, and AI-coordinated multi-step remediation workflows.
what_to_verify_publicly: AI-autonomous resolution of defined incident classes
Adaptive response selection based on incident context
AI-coordinated multi-step remediation workflows
Reduction in human intervention for resolved incidents
Guardrails and human-in-the-loop controls for AI responses

AIO-04.name: AI Transparency & Explainability
AIO-04.expanded_definition: Transparency and explainability of AI-driven decisions within the MDR service - including human-readable explanations for AI actions, audit trails for automated decisions, and clear documentation of when and why AI intervened versus human analysts.
what_to_verify_publicly: Explainable AI outputs with human-readable reasoning
Audit trail for AI-automated actions and decisions
Clear delineation between AI and human-driven actions in reports
Client-facing documentation of AI capabilities and limitations
Quality metrics for AI outputs (hallucination rates, accuracy)

AID-01.name: Domain-Specific AI/LLM Investment
AID-01.expanded_definition: Vendor investment in security-specific AI models and domain-specific LLMs - not merely wrapping generic foundation models but developing or fine-tuning models on security-specific training data for detection, investigation, and threat intelligence tasks.
what_to_verify_publicly: Named domain-specific AI models or security LLMs
Evidence of security-specific model training or fine-tuning
Documented AI/ML engineering team and investment
Published research, patents, or conference presentations on security AI
Differentiation from generic GPT-wrapper implementations

AID-02.name: AI Model Governance & Lifecycle
AID-02.expanded_definition: Governance of AI models used within the MDR service - including model versioning, testing and validation before deployment, performance monitoring, drift detection, and retirement procedures to ensure consistent, trustworthy AI outputs.
what_to_verify_publicly: Model versioning and lifecycle management practices
Pre-deployment testing and validation procedures
Production model performance monitoring and drift detection
Model update cadence and change management processes
AI incident response for model failures or degradation

AID-03.name: AI Supply Chain & Trustworthiness
AID-03.expanded_definition: Assurance of the AI supply chain within the MDR service - including provenance of foundation models, third-party AI component risk assessment, training data governance, and controls to prevent model compromise or poisoning.
what_to_verify_publicly: Foundation model provenance and supply chain documentation
Third-party AI component risk assessment processes
Training data governance and quality assurance
Model security controls (prompt injection defense, adversarial testing)
Compliance with AI trustworthiness frameworks (NIST AI RMF, EU AI Act)

AID-04.name: AI-Driven Service Innovation
AID-04.expanded_definition: Evidence of AI-driven innovation that extends the MDR service beyond traditional capabilities - including new service offerings enabled by AI, expanded coverage through AI efficiency, and investment in emerging AI applications for security operations.
what_to_verify_publicly: New service capabilities or offerings enabled by AI
Expanded coverage or service scope through AI efficiency
AI innovation pipeline with named features or products
Client-visible AI improvements in service quality over time
AI-enabled differentiation from competitors

SOG-01.name: 24/7 SOC Coverage & Analyst Model
SOG-01.expanded_definition: The operational foundation of the MDR service - including geographic distribution of SOC operations, analyst tier structure, named or dedicated resources, and the human staffing model that ensures continuous, qualified coverage.
what_to_verify_publicly: 24/7/365 SOC operations with documented geographic coverage
Analyst tier structure (L1/L2/L3) with defined responsibilities
Dedicated or named analyst model (e.g., concierge security team)
Analyst qualification and certification requirements
Staff retention rates and experience level documentation

SOG-02.name: Client Engagement & Transparency
SOG-02.expanded_definition: The client-facing engagement model - including onboarding processes, regular business reviews, escalation paths, communication transparency, and the overall client experience framework that builds trust and ensures alignment with business objectives.
what_to_verify_publicly: Structured onboarding process with documented timeline
Regular business review cadence (monthly, quarterly)
Named client contacts with clear escalation paths
Client portal or dashboard for real-time visibility
Satisfaction measurement and feedback mechanisms

SOG-03.name: Compliance & Regulatory Alignment
SOG-03.expanded_definition: The compliance posture of the MDR service - including vendor certifications, regulatory framework alignment, data handling practices, and support for client compliance requirements in regulated industries.
what_to_verify_publicly: SOC 2 Type II certification (or equivalent)
ISO 27001 certification
Support for regulated industry requirements (healthcare, finance, government)
Data residency and sovereignty controls
Compliance reporting capabilities for client audits

SOG-04.name: Reporting Quality & Metrics
SOG-04.expanded_definition: Quality and depth of service reporting - including actionable executive summaries, technical incident reports, trend analysis, performance metrics, and ROI-oriented reporting that demonstrates the value and impact of the MDR service.
what_to_verify_publicly: Executive-level reporting with business impact context
Technical incident reports with detailed analysis
Trend analysis and threat landscape reporting
Performance metrics dashboards with KPI tracking
ROI and value demonstration reporting

pricing_evaluation.description: Separate evaluation scale assessing the maturity and transparency of the vendor's pricing model, based on Gartner's composable pricing research. This is NOT a capability assessment - it evaluates how well the vendor's commercial construct serves buyer and provider interests.
pricing_evaluation.framework_source: Gartner Research: 'Pricing Constructs That Support Profitable Business Process Services Revenue' (G00826132, April 2025) and 'Outcome-Based Pricing Fails Tech CEOs in Services' (G00846386, February 2026)

PRC-SUB.name: Subscription Transparency
PRC-SUB.definition: Clarity and structure of recurring subscription fees - including breakdown of human analyst time, platform access fees, AI tool fees, managed service bundles, and non-AI software components.
what_to_evaluate: Published subscription pricing tiers or structure
Component breakdown visible to buyers (human time vs. platform vs. AI)
Predictability of recurring costs for client budgeting
Flexibility in subscription scope adjustment
Transparency about what is included vs. excluded
PRC-SUB.pricing_model_alignment: Subscriptions provide the revenue floor and budget predictability. Applicable to Standard TDIR, Disinformation Security monitoring, and Deception-as-a-Service where continuous human-in-the-loop oversight and baseline platform access are required.

PRC-USG.name: Usage-Based Alignment
PRC-USG.definition: Variable cost components driven by actual consumption - including API calls, data volume ingested, compute hours, AI inference charges, and overages - with transparent measurement and real-time tracking.
what_to_evaluate: Usage-based pricing components clearly defined
Measurement systems for quantifying consumption
Real-time usage dashboards or monitoring available to clients
Clear overage policies and escalation thresholds
Alignment of usage fees with computational effort provided
PRC-USG.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to Preemptive Threat Intelligence - AI compute, data volume, and inference charges align cost to computational effort. Also relevant for cloud-based telemetry ingestion.

PRC-FIX.name: Fixed Delivery Pricing
PRC-FIX.definition: One-time costs for discrete scope items - including initial deployment, integration setup, customized playbook creation, deception environment design, and complex telemetry pipeline implementation.
what_to_evaluate: Clear one-time fees defined for setup and implementation
Scope definition for fixed-fee deliverables
Separation of project costs from ongoing service costs
Change request and scope adjustment processes
Implementation timeline and milestone-based payment structure
PRC-FIX.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to initial deployment of Autonomous Deception and AMTD environments, complex telemetry integrations, and customized AI playbook creation.

PRC-SUC.name: Success & Outcome Fees
PRC-SUC.definition: Performance-linked pricing components - including bonuses, penalties, or per-unit fees based on achieving engagement objectives, MTTD/MTTR targets, or AI-automated resolution metrics. Includes fees-at-risk mechanisms.
what_to_evaluate: Defined success metrics tied to pricing (MTTD, MTTR, resolution rates)
Fees-at-risk component in service agreements
Per-resolution or per-unit pricing for AI-automated outcomes
Clear measurement methodology and dispute resolution
Balance of risk between provider and client
PRC-SUC.pricing_model_alignment: Applicable to Standard TDIR and AI Automations - per-resolution fees for AI-automated incident classes, and success bonuses tied to verified MTTD/MTTR reductions. Must balance Gartner's caution that outcome-based pricing often fails due to measurement complexity.

PRC-COM.name: Composability & Overall Model Maturity
PRC-COM.definition: Overall maturity of the pricing model as a composable, transparent hybrid - assessing whether the vendor's commercial construct can be assembled and reassembled to suit client needs, protects revenue while balancing risk, and avoids the pitfalls of pure outcome-based pricing.
what_to_evaluate: Multiple pricing components available and combinable
Client budgeting predictability with spending expectations set upfront
Demonstrated risk-sharing with clear rewards and penalties
Avoidance of excessive variability and dispute potential
Demystification of what the client pays for, when, and why
PRC-COM.pricing_model_alignment: The composable approach is the Gartner-recommended best practice - a 'best-of-breed' combination that protects provider revenue, enhances client position, balances risk, and avoids the failure modes of pure outcome-based pricing.

PRC-OUT.name: Pricing-to-Outcomes Alignment
PRC-OUT.definition: Assessment of how well the vendor's pricing model is aligned to measurable client outcomes - evaluating whether pricing components are tied to demonstrated business value, security outcomes, and operational improvements rather than purely input-based (seats, volume, hours). This dimension may complement or conflict with the other pricing dimensions depending on the vendor's maturity.
what_to_evaluate: Pricing components explicitly tied to measurable security outcomes (MTTD/MTTR reduction, breach prevention, risk reduction)
Outcome-based SLA commitments with financial consequences (credits, rebates, penalties)
Value realization metrics shared with clients showing pricing-to-outcome correlation
Pricing adjustments based on demonstrated AI efficiency gains passed to clients
Avoidance of outcome-washing - pricing labeled as outcome-based but measured on inputs
PRC-OUT.pricing_model_alignment: Gartner research cautions that pure outcome-based pricing frequently fails due to measurement complexity and dispute potential. This dimension evaluates whether vendors have found a sustainable middle ground - tying pricing components to verifiable outcomes without creating unsustainable risk for either party. The most mature vendors embed outcome alignment within a composable model rather than making it the entire commercial construct.
PRC-OUT.complementarity_note: PRC-OUT may be complementary to other pricing dimensions (e.g., a vendor with strong PRC-SUB and PRC-SUC that also aligns fees to outcomes) or it may stand alone. Vendors scoring high on PRC-COM but low on PRC-OUT have composable pricing without outcome linkage. Vendors scoring high on PRC-OUT but low on PRC-COM have outcome ambitions without composable structure.

outcome_maturity_rating.description: Overall maturity rating for the vendor's alignment of pricing to business outcomes. This is NOT a pricing score - it evaluates the holistic maturity of the vendor's ability to demonstrate, measure, and align their commercial model to verifiable client outcomes across the MDR engagement lifecycle.
outcome_maturity_rating.framework_source: Derived from Gartner Research: 'Outcome-Based Pricing Fails Tech CEOs in Services' (G00846386, February 2026) and MDR market evolution toward value-based commercial models.

scoring_logic.0: No Evidence: No public information about outcome linkage in pricing or service delivery.
scoring_logic.1: Input-Only: Pricing is entirely input-based (per-seat, per-device, per-GB). No outcome metrics referenced in commercial constructs. Service value is assumed, not measured.
scoring_logic.2: Outcome-Aware: Vendor references outcomes (MTTD/MTTR improvement, risk reduction) in marketing but pricing model is not structurally linked to those outcomes. SLAs may exist but lack financial consequences.
scoring_logic.3: Outcome-Linked: Specific pricing components are tied to measurable outcomes. SLAs have financial consequences (credits, rebates). Value realization reporting demonstrates pricing-to-outcome correlation, though measurement methodology may be vendor-controlled.
scoring_logic.4: Outcome-Validated: Pricing model embeds verified outcome metrics with independent or jointly agreed measurement. Client-visible dashboards show real-time outcome performance. Pricing adjustments (up or down) occur based on demonstrated value delivery. Risk-sharing is balanced and documented.
scoring_logic.5: Outcome-Native: The entire commercial model is designed around verifiable outcome delivery with transparent measurement, balanced risk-sharing, AI-efficiency gain pass-through to clients, and continuous value optimization. Pricing, SLAs, and service delivery form an integrated outcome engine. Rare in current market - represents the theoretical ideal.

evaluation_criteria: Does the vendor's pricing change based on outcomes delivered (not just inputs consumed)?
Are outcome metrics independently verifiable or solely vendor-reported?
Does the vendor share AI-driven efficiency gains with clients through pricing adjustments?
Is outcome alignment embedded in the contract structure or limited to marketing claims?
Does the vendor demonstrate a track record of outcome-based client renewals and expansions?
Are outcome metrics aligned with the ROI measurement framework KPIs defined in this schema?

roi_measurement_framework.description: Key performance indicators for measuring the ROI of AI-augmented MDR services. Focus shifts from cost savings to evaluating enhancements in speed, service quality, and expanded operational scope.

speed_metrics.name: Detection & Response Speed
kpis: Mean Time to Detect (MTTD) reduction percentage
Mean Time to Respond (MTTR) reduction percentage
SLA adherence rate for detection and response phases

autonomy_metrics.name: Resolution Autonomy & Efficiency
kpis: Percentage of incidents resolved without client intervention
Volume of required client clarifications per month
AI autonomous resolution rate for defined incident classes

coverage_metrics.name: Expanded Visibility & Coverage
kpis: Percentage increase in alerts investigated vs. baseline
Number of telemetry sources and asset types covered
Expansion to new use cases or threat categories

quality_metrics.name: Alert & Output Quality
kpis: AI hallucination or degraded output incidents
Quality of investigation reports and recommendations

resource_metrics.name: Internal Resource Impact
kpis: Internal analyst time freed for higher-value tasks
Analyst upskilling enabled by AI-augmented workflows

impact_metrics.name: Business Impact KPIs
kpis: Reputation damage prevention for disinformation threats
Regulatory penalty avoidance through compliance alignment
